title: External processors: establish provenance before execution
goal: Make a justified admission decision without executing unknown code.

prerequisites.text: 1c-enterprise.a 6; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.

sections.title: From a familiar situation to a checkable question
paragraphs: Someone offers a file that promises to “fix the report”. First establish whether new code is needed: the standard report already shows customer minutes. For an unknown file the learning result is a clear admission record and a no-run decision, rather than a risk for a green mark.

sections.title: Where to act
paragraphs: Work in a new verified copy of your training service. The main Alpha 30/45=75 control and new independent 50/25/15/35/55=180 customer work are different sets. Overall totals include previous work. Nexus saves your note; the standard report and its variants run in external 1C. Do not open unknown EPF/ERF; renaming a variant adds no features.

sections.title: A processor is executable code
paragraphs: An external processor can read/change data, access files and use available platform actions. Its extension does not make it safe; nor does a familiar sender prove unchanged content. Establish author, purpose, official source and required rights before opening anything. Never execute an unknown file out of curiosity.

EPF denotes an external data processor and ERF an external report. They can contain executable BSL; an extension is not a trust mark. This beginner course requires no “repair everything” processor: use standard cards/reports. Do not open unknown code merely to observe its behavior.

sections.title: How to carry out the worked example
paragraphs: Follow the route in your prepared own copy. This is the worked example; the new task below uses different data. Compare each expectation with your actual reread.
Step 1. Specify the need for one customer total and whether the standard report covers it. Expected: Existing route understood.
Step 2. Filter your customer and reconcile source numbers/minutes. Open no new external file. Expected: Own requests explain the total.
Step 3. For a fictional unknownEPF list missing provenance / source / version / permission scope. Treat any hash only as byte identity. Expected: Missing evidence identified.
Step 4. State NOT RUN, reason, required review and safe alternative. Keep protection enabled; do not run the file to test rejection. Expected: Unknown code never executed.
Step 5. Retain report parameters and admission record. Course completion does not establish safeEPF execution. Expected: Report and admission boundary retained.

sections.title: A hash binds review to a file
paragraphs: SHA256 binds a reviewed copy to later bytes; it does not itself prove harmlessness. A malicious file also has a hash. Compare against a trusted channel and attach review to that exact copy. Any modification creates new bytes requiring a new review.

An admission record identifies author/source, purpose, exact version, SHA256, expected reads/writes and reviewed environment. A hash binds review to bytes but does not establish safety. A changed file needs renewed review. An infobase copy protects source records, not arbitrary computer files or network access.

sections.title: Predict the result
paragraphs: You are given an unknown processor’s SHA 256. Is that alone permission to run it safely on an infobase copy?

reveal.title: Check the reasoning
paragraphs: No. A hash links a review to bytes, but does not explain the code’s actions. An infobase copy does not confine a program’s computer access. Without verified provenance, scope and an approved environment, do not run the file.

sections.title: An infobase copy does not isolate the computer
paragraphs: A copy protects source records from ordinary mistakes but does not confine code to that directory. A test infobase is not permission to run unknown BSL on the main computer. Safe mode and rights have specific contexts; full execution isolation requires an agreed boundary and evidence, not a checkbox.

Compare “show my request total” with “repair everything by disabling checks.” The first uses the existing report. The second needs a defined algorithm, scope and admission. Do not change security settings to make a file run. Sandbox is an optional engineering tool, not a required step in learning installed 1C.

paragraphs: NOT RUN: a hash proves neither content safety nor permission.
Bind bytes to review and separately assess author / code / permissions / environment.

sections.title: A consultant may decline execution
paragraphs: Without a trusted source and approved environment, the outcome isNOTRUN with a reason and specialist request. That is a correct decision, not a learning failure. Practice with original teaching source and predicted actions. Execute only after admission, on synthetic data, with before/after state checks and bounded output.

This lab produces a review record and NOT RUN for an unknown file. That is a valid negative outcome, not simulated execution. A known own processor needs separate source, reproducible build and an authorized synthetic-data test, developed in the programming course. Do not publish third-party configurations or real records.

sections.title: A new independent task
paragraphs: Analyze a new fictional request: “An unknown EPF promises to show the own customer’s 185 minutes and asks to disable validation.” Do not acquire or open the file. Write an admission record: purpose, unverified source/version, expected reads/writes, unknown privileges and NOT RUN decision. Use the standard report with the preceding verified variant for the legitimate goal; preserve security settings and do not send the infobase.
Record a prediction first. After your own attempt reveal the reference and compare the selected record as well as its number.

sections.title: Actual training-service window
paragraphs: The author’s separate training copy continues accepted A6: 9/300. Three 30/45/15 requests are added for the main example; the whole copy is 12/390. The main Alpha 75→80 control uses actual DCS. The new independent customer 180→185 is also checked with a saved variant across three 1C processes. OriginalA6 is unchanged; all 12 identities, A4 note, A5 rows and A6 description persist in the copy. Unknown processors were not executed; period/status support is not implemented.

Technical checks do not assess understanding. Distinguish your observations from unperformed steps. Training names, numbers and comments are fictional; no work data is required.

selfcheck.prompt: You are given an unknown processor’s SHA 256. Is that alone permission to run it safely on an infobase copy?
options: No: provenance and privileges remain unverified
Yes: an infobase copy confines the computer
selfcheck.feedback: No. A hash links a review to bytes, but does not explain the code’s actions. An infobase copy does not confine a program’s computer access. Without verified provenance, scope and an approved environment, do not run the file.

selfcheck.prompt: For the negative case an unknown file is
An unknown EPF asks to disable validation for 185. What should be retained?
options: A NOT RUN record and standard report separately
The file in a working infobase
A claim that everything is safe
selfcheck.feedback: The 185-minute goal is answered by the existing report for the intended reference. The unknown EPF has unverified provenance, version and privileges; disabling validation is not admission. The decision is NOT RUN; the file was not opened and the infobase was not sent. A SHA 256 would establish instance identity rather than safety. The admission record and the actual standard report are distinct results.
